learningObjectives: Relate architecture, objective, data, backpropagated gradients, optimization, and evaluation without treating any one as the whole learning system.
Distinguish Rosenblatt's historical perceptron program from the narrower later textbook linear classifier.
Explain how hidden representations become task-useful under backpropagation and why usefulness does not guarantee causal truth or interpretability.
Identify local connectivity and weight sharing as architectural priors in convolutional document recognition rather than discoveries made from data alone.
definitions: Artificial neural network: a parameterized composition of connected computational units, not by that name a faithful biological model.
Backpropagation: reverse application of the chain rule that computes an objective's derivatives with respect to intermediate quantities and parameters.
Representation: an internal transformation or encoding used by later computations in a learned system.
Weight sharing: use of the same learned parameters at multiple positions or relations.
Architectural prior: a constraint or symmetry encoded in the model's available computations before training data are fitted.
notebookPrompt: Create an advanced source-grounded explainer titled ‘Neural Networks, Backpropagation, and Representation Learning.’ Organize it around a relational diagram connecting architecture, data, objective, backpropagated gradients, optimization path, internal representation, evaluation, and deployment. Use Rosenblatt to recover the perceptron as a historical adaptive-organization program without equating it to all modern networks. Use Rumelhart, Hinton, and Williams to explain how error derivatives give hidden units task-dependent learning signals while explicitly acknowledging the longer differentiation lineage. Use LeCun, Bottou, Bengio, and Haffner to show how local connectivity, weight sharing, subsampling, structured task constraints, and end-to-end learning cooperate in document recognition. Use Bengio, Courville, and Vincent to frame representation learning as a plural research program with unresolved criteria. Include negative controls: gradients are not explanations, learned does not mean undesigned, benchmark recognition is not general perception, and useful features are not necessarily causal or transferable. Do not narrate a single-hero invention story.
humanFrame: Show that neural learning moves design among relations rather than abolishing it. Preserve historical terminology, priority uncertainty, and task scope.
assessment: Given a trained image classifier, identify which properties came from architecture, data, objective, optimization, and evaluation; then reject two claims about interpretability or general intelligence that do not follow.
